question: Why are North rentals down on last year since May?
answer:
I'll analyze the North region data to understand why rentals are down since May compared to last year.

## Year-over-Year Comparison (North Total)

| Week | 2025 (prior year) | 2026 (current) | Change | % Change |
|------|-------------------|----------------|--------|----------|
| Early period (Apr 7 - May 4) | ~4,700 avg | ~4,600 avg | roughly flat | ~-2% |
| **May 4 onwards** | | | | |
| May 4 | 4,676 | 4,686 | +10 | +0.2% |
| May 11 | 5,193 | 4,494 | **-699** | **-13.5%** |
| May 18 | 5,030 | 4,933 | -97 | -1.9% |
| May 25 | 5,185 | 4,642 | **-543** | **-10.5%** |
| Jun 1 | 5,069 | 4,931 | -138 | -2.7% |
| Jun 8 | 5,532 | 4,638 | **-894** | **-16.2%** |
| Jun 15 | 5,672 | 4,787 | **-885** | **-15.6%** |
| Jun 22 | 5,451 | 5,038 | -413 | -7.6% |

## Key Finding: The Timing Matches the Price Change

**North region new list prices went live on 2026-05-04** (per the price list changes and confirmed by staff note from S. Marrin at D01 on 2026-04-28: *"New list prices for the North go live Monday 4 May"*).

## Evidence of Price Sensitivity

The staff note from **2026-05-19 at D02 Petherby (North)** is particularly telling:
> *"Several regulars grumbling about the new prices. Two said they would shop around."*

This directly indicates **customer pushback and potential lost business to competitors** following the price increase.

## Depot-Level Breakdown (May-June period)

| Depot | 2025 avg (May-Jun) | 2026 avg (May-Jun) | Change |
|-------|-------------------|-------------------|--------|
| D01 Hollin Cross | ~2,150 | ~1,960 | **-8.8%** |
| D02 Petherby | ~1,470 | ~1,360 | **-7.5%** |
| D03 Scarrow Bridge | ~1,590 | ~1,460 | **-8.2%** |

All three North depots show declines, with **D01 Hollin Cross (the largest depot) down most in absolute terms**.

## Conclusion

**North rentals are down since May primarily because of the new list price implementation on 4 May 2026.** The timing is exact:
- April 2026: roughly flat vs. prior year
- May 2026 onwards: consistent 8-16% declines vs. prior year
- Staff explicitly report customer complaints and threats to "shop around"

The prior year (2025) also shows a seasonal uplift from May onwards (peaking in June), which makes the 2026 decline even more pronounced — the expected seasonal growth didn't materialize, suggesting the price increase suppressed demand that would normally have grown.
